summary: How Tech Works: made and shipped the long video L-20261124-21 'How Does ASML's EUV Machine Print a Chip With Light?' (428 s, 64 directed 3D beats in 10 places), from the owner's first pinned topic (EUV lithography).
why: state --format long said video (1 of 3 long videos this week). The fact review passed after one rewrite: the main pulse comes from the same laser, and plasma atoms lose some of their electrons, not all. QA passed on its third look: round 1 had 6 blocking items, round 2 had 1 (three camera moves that looked at nothing), and all were fixed. Every render gate passed.

findings.title: Thumbnails
findings.detail: Pick B 'Printed by plasma' (9/10); A 'No lenses' (8/10); C 'Tin to chip' (8/10). QA would click C, then B. Run Test & Compare with all three.

findings.title: Length needed about 1,330 words
findings.detail: The estimated voice runs ~14% short. 1,154 words gave 408 s, under the 420 s minimum, so 8 beats were added (all fact-checked) to reach 428 s.

findings.title: QA notes left open (not blocking)
findings.detail: The source chip reads 'ASML · ASML (EUV lithography systems)' because the two feed facts name the source differently. There is no ASML logo on the machine. 125 s / 135 s and 250 s / 265 s look alike. The audio mean is -16.3 dB, against a -18 dB target.

changes.title: Shipped L-20261124-21
changes.detail: Manifest on main (02b2aa2); the mp4 went up on media/L-20261124-21 for the release workflow. The full render took about 6.5 h (11 chunks).
